sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Specialty Fresh Bakery Master Franchise and Central Kitchen Ops

stage_1.document_name: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal / Certificate of Good Standing of the corporate shareholder (Chinese parent)
stage_1.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of the People's Republic of China / competent local market supervision bureau
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille — Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (PRC) or authorised provincial foreign-affairs office; then sworn Spanish translation and Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Colombia reception (no Colombian consular legalization required)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (S.A.S. regime), Articles 2, 3, 5, 17 and 25; Código de Comercio (Decreto Ley 410/1971) Articles 110–129; Decreto 1074/2015 (mercantile registry consolidation); municipal tariffs per annual Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio rate schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the corporate domicile (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá) through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES); supervised by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) signed by all shareholders, optionally authenticated before a Notary where real property is contributed; filed with the RUES as the constitutive registration act (inscripción constitutiva).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital under Law 1258/2008. The bylaws set the subscribed and paid-in capital; payment may be deferred in accordance with the bylaws. No escrow account is required; inbound capital contributions by non-resident shareholders must be registered with Banco de la República under the foreign-exchange regime and channelled through authorized intermediaries.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION No. 01 OF THE SOLE INCORPORATOR AND SOLE SHAREHOLDER OF [COMPANY] S.A.S.

The sole incorporator, acting under Article 5 of Law 1258 of 2008, resolves:

FIRST: To approve the private incorporation document and bylaws of [Company] S.A.S., domiciled in Bogotá D.C.
SECOND: To subscribe and fully pay share capital of COP [X], represented by [X] ordinary shares of no par value; no minimum capital is required by law.
THIRD: To adopt the registered office at [address].
FOURTH: To appoint [NAME] as Manager and Legal Representative and [NAME] as Alternate Manager.
FIFTH: To authorize the Manager to effect registration before the Chamber of Commerce, the DIAN, and other competent authorities and to sign ancillary instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reserve and Homonimia Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio of proposed domicile via RUES online portal (www.rues.org.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the RUES user portal, submit up to three proposed corporate names with the stated business purpose (ISIC 5610 / NAICS 722515 bakery and central kitchen), and obtain the 'certificado de homonimia'. Confirm the selected name quarantine for 30 business days. The name reservation is mandatory before drafting the incorporation instrument.
required_dossiers: Tax/foreign tax identification and passport or citizenship card of each constituent shareholder
Proposed corporate name and principal purpose declaration
Corporate contact email and mobile number
Power of attorney if the filing is made by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected for similarity, resubmit alternative names; a 'recurso de reposición' at the same Chamber is available within 10 days where the prior registration precedent is challengable. A fresh reservation period starts upon each accepted alternative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Private Incorporation Instrument and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Constituent shareholders or lawful attorney-in-fact; optional authentication before a Notary Public if real estate is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución pursuant to Article 5, Law 1258/2008, containing all mandatory content of Article 17: shareholders, capital subscription table, share class, payment terms, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, and audit provisions. All shareholders execute the deed; contributions of real property must be formalized by public deed and entered in the property register.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate (homonimia)
Identity documents/passports of shareholders and legal representative
Power of attorney if signed by an agent
Final bylaws and capital subscription schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial or legal counsel identifies defects in the charter, execute a corrective 'aclaratoria' or restate the instrument as a public deed before the same Notary; the corrected document is submitted together with the original until registration is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RUT Pre-Registration and Commercial Registry Filing (Matrícula Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio – Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) / RUES; pre-registration is exchanged with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the RUES forms and the pre-RUT with DIAN, submitting the signed private instrument, payment of 'derechos de inscripción' and attention rate ('cuota de RUES'). Once admitted, the Chamber assigns the corporate folio and issues the Commercial Registration Certificate ('certificado de existencia y representación legal'); legal personality is born as of this inscription. Verify that the CIIU 5610 code and central kitchen/bakery chain activities are noted, and apply for the municipal industry and commerce tax (ICA) registration at the relevant Treasury.
required_dossiers: Signed Documento Privado de Constitución
RUES single registration forms (matrícula mercantil de sociedad y de establecimientos)
Pre-formulated RUT and NIT pre-assignment
Payment receipts of Chamber tariff
Identification of manager and alternate manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber raises an observation, the company must file a corrective minute within 30 days; failure to do so cancels the filing. Objections may be answered by amending the bylaws and resubmitting through the same RUES window; administrative recourses under Ley 1437/2011 apply thereafter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive Tax Registrations: NIT/RUT with DIAN and Municipal Taxes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (www.dian.gov.co) and municipal Secretaría de Hacienda for ICA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the commercial registration is certified, update the RUT electronically: activate the definitive NIT, assign tax attributes (income tax responsible; standard-rated VAT for bakery retail and POS, central kitchen operations may involve zero-rated export sales if cross-border to other countries), obtain the digital electronic-invoicing certificate, and establish the December 31 accounting close. Register for the ICA tax with the municipal Treasury and request the 'registro de contribuyentes industriales y comerciales' at the city where each branch operates.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration certificate issued by the Chamber
Pre-RUT form and final RUT with DIAN
Identity and electronic signature (certificado digital) of the legal representative
ICA municipal registration application per branch/central kitchen address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT is incorrect or flagged ('objeción al RUT'), file an electronic correction before DIAN, selecting 'actualización de RUT' with the supporting certificate; if blocked, attend a DIAN point of contact with the corporate certificate to obtain reactivation within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance: First Board Resolution and Legalization of Corporate Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate assembly (sole shareholder or board); Cámara de Comercio for legalization of the merchant books
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting and adopt the First Board Resolution (see pro forma above) appointing the Manager and Alternate Manager, approving the capitalization and the registered office, and authorizing licensing filings. Prepare the corporate minutes book ('libro de actas') and shareholders register ('libro de registro de accionistas'), then present them to the Chamber for sealing/legalization before any entries are made; complete appointment of the statutory auditor ('revisor fiscal') if the company exceeds the statutory thresholds for a bakery-chain central kitchen.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution signed by the shareholders or organizer
Commercial registration certificate
Shareholder registry with share issuance dates and capital payment records
Company NIT
Notification of statutory-auditor appointment (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber refuses to legalize books due to formal defects, issue an amended act and resubmit; late legalization is still admissible, although minutes executed before sealing bear reduced evidentiary value and may expose the manager to civil liability under the Código de Comercio.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sanitary Registration, Municipal Operating License and Land-Use Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INVIMA (food sanitary registration); Secretaría de Salud of the municipality ('concepto sanitario'); Alcaldía/Curaduría Urbana (land use and business operating permit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the technical dossier ('expediente tecnológico') for bakery/chinese pastry products under INVIMA risk classification, including formulas, ingredient declarations, packaging and labeling drafts, facility blueprints and a GMP/HACCP schedule. Obtain the municipal health concept and the 'licencia de funcionamiento' or land-use permit for each bakery retail point and the central kitchen. Open the establishment only after favorable opinions are issued.
required_dossiers: RUT and commercial registration certificate
Complete INVIMA technical file (formulation, packaging, labeling, hazard analysis)
Central-kitchen floor plans, equipment list and cleaning/sanitation program
Land-use and occupancy certificates (uso de suelo) for each premises
Public water and wastewater service provider contracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If INVIMA issues a deficiency report ('auto de requerimiento'), respond within the granted term (typically 20 days) with amended technical documents; if the permit is denied, file an administrative appeal (recurso de reposición, then subsidiar apelación) under Ley 1437/2011; in parallel, correct the health concept through re-inspection of the bakery floor.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Permits, Discharge and Emissions Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) of the jurisdiction; municipal Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente for larger cities; ANLA only if project scale exceeds national thresholds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a bakery and central kitchen classified in the low environmental impact category, file a declaration of no environmental license requirement ('no sujeción a licencia'); secure a wastewater discharge permit ('permiso de vertimientos') if the central kitchen discharges industrial loads, and an atrium emissions exemption or 'permiso de emisiones atmosféricas' for ovens above threshold. Contract licensed haulers for used frying oil and organic waste and maintain environmental-compliance logbooks.
required_dossiers: Oven and boiler technical specifications and fuel certification
Wastewater characterization report (BOD5, TSS, pH, fats-oils-greases) if discharging to sewer
Contracts with environmental licensed waste management providers
Copy of municipal land-use and construction permits
Environmental compliance register/declaration forms of the CAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If classified outside the exemption band, prepare an environmental diagnosis with a Plan de Manejo Ambiental for CAR approval; appeal any adverse classification under Ley 1437/2011 and adjust the technical parameters (e.g., grease traps, oven filters) to meet municipal sewer ordinances, then request a revised inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - national tax and customs authority. Portal: https://www.dian.gov.co; transactional platform: https://muisca.dian.gov.co (MUISCA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the S.A.S. deed of incorporation before a Colombian notary; non-resident shareholders act through a legal representative or apoderado holding an apostilled power of attorney. Step 2: Register the company with the local Cámara de Comercio to obtain commercial registration. Step 3: Register in the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) via MUISCA using the representative's digital certificate; DIAN assigns the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria), which concurrently operates as the corporate tax ID, VAT ID and customs ID. Step 4: Select tax responsibilities in the RUT, including mandatory responsibilities for corporate income tax (renta), IVA (Responsable del Régimen Común) and electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica, code 35). Step 5: Where the non-resident parent receives Colombian-source amounts prior to entity formation, the parent must itself obtain a NIT through a Colombian fiscal representative to avoid excess withholding.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope: the S.A.S. is a separate Colombian corporate tax resident; income tax operates under the source rule (Arts. 12-13 E.T.) with Colombian-source business income taxed at the general 35% corporate rate, and non-resident shareholders bear additional dividend taxation at distribution under Arts. 242-245 E.T. No pass-through treatment is available to an S.A.S.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (i) SIMPLE tax regime (Arts. 903-916 E.T.): optional combined income-plus-IVA regime for an S.A.S. whose annual gross income does not exceed 100,000 UVT; election is made in the RUT by the date DIAN indicates. (ii) Transfer pricing documentation elections (Art. 260-1 E.T.): selection of the transactional profit method used in the local and master file. (iii) Anti-hybrid and GAAR rules (Arts. 118-1 et seq. E.T. per Law 2010/2019) allow re-characterization of mismatched cross-border payments, but Colombia has no check-the-box election. (iv) Optional e-invoicing authorization as 'proveedor tecnológico' (Resolution 000165/2023) is available for group service companies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre las Ventas (IVA) - Colombian national value added tax, Arts. 420-512 E.T.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary de minimis for corporations: the S.A.S. must register as IVA-responsible (Régimen Común) in the RUT from its first taxable supply of bakery goods and services, regardless of turnover (Decree 1625/2016, Art. 1.6.1.2.1). The optional SIMPLE regime is available only where annual gross income does not exceed 100,000 UVT (COP 4,979,900,000 for FY2025, UVT 2025 = COP 49,799); above this ceiling, traditional IVA and income tax reporting is mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing ('Factura Electrónica de Venta', FEV) per DIAN Resolution 000165/2023: the S.A.S. must issue XML invoices through a DIAN-authorized technology provider and submit them to MUISCA for pre-validation ('validación previa') via SOAP/REST web services; the approved invoice is stamped with a CUNE code and QR before delivery to the customer. Export transactions require an export-type electronic invoice with incoterms and customs-office data. Non-compliance blocks the counterparty's input VAT credit and triggers sanctions under Arts. 652 and 652-13 E.T.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to (a) tangible goods physically exported when evidenced by the DEX customs declaration, and (b) services exports under Art. 481 E.T. if: the buyer has no residence/domicile in Colombia, the service is used exclusively outside Colombia (e.g., offshore master-franchise know-how, royalties and central-kitchen technical assistance), the consideration is paid by the non-resident without Colombian intermediary intervention, and the service is declared as an export in MUISCA. Local franchise sales attract 19% IVA, except basic basket items (e.g., bread) excluded at 0% under Art. 424 E.T.; pastries and confectionery are standard-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DEX - Declaración de Exportación (approved customs export declaration issued via MUISCA)
Bill of Lading (BL) or Airway Bill (AWB) evidencing physical exit of goods
Certificado de cambio / Formulario No. 4 (Declaración de Cambio por Exportaciones de Bienes) issued by the Colombian intermediary bank evidencing FX repatriation
Commercial export invoice matching the DEX in value, quantity and incoterms
For services exports: certificate of non-residence of the buyer, the executed service/license agreement, and delivery evidence showing exclusive use abroad
Packing list and inspection/certificate of origin where required by destination customs
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Exporters' VAT refunds (saldo a favor) are subject to accelerated DIAN verification (30 working days under Art. 855 E.T. if the complete documentation bundle is filed; refunds prescribe after 5 years). False or inflated export claims trigger: (i) the 100% inexactness penalty on the difference or refund improperly obtained (Art. 648 E.T.); (ii) moratory interest under Art. 635 E.T. from the refund application date; (iii) retroactive clawback of the principal plus interest through official correction within the 5-year statute of limitations; (iv) criminal tax fraud under Arts. 434A-434G of the Criminal Code (imprisonment of 48-108 months where evasion exceeds 400 monthly minimum legal wages, approximately COP 586M for FY2025); and (v) cancellation of the RUT and prohibition on issuing export invoices for recidivist false exporters.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (the Central Bank of the Republic of Colombia), acting in coordination with the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit and the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) as the supervisory authorities for the organized foreign-exchange market. The governing framework comprises Law 9 of 1991, the Central External Regulation DCIN 83 (adopting Resolution No. 8 of 2000 and its subsequent amendments), Decree 1068 of 2015, and the SFC's SARLAFT and foreign-exchange compliance circulars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a managed-floating regime for the Colombian peso (COP). Current-account transactions, including goods exports, service fees, royalties, interest and dividends, are generally convertible and free from prior central-bank licensing, but transactions at or above the USD 10,000 threshold must be channeled through an authorized FX market intermediary and supported by a Declaración de Cambio. Capital-account flows, particularly inbound foreign direct investment into the CO_SAS and eventual equity or capital repatriation, are not subject to prior government approval but are mandatorily registrable with Banco de la República through the intermediary bank under the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales. Profit-remittance hurdles for the non-resident franchisor/shareholder include the proper legalization of the original FDI registration before any dividend equals USD 10,000 or more is wired abroad, the full payment of Colombian corporate income tax on distributable earnings, the application of the statutory dividend withholding for non-resident shareholders, the production of the corporate distribution resolution and audited financial statements, and the obligation to route the remittance through the registered local bank account using the correct exchange concept account. Any unregistered, fragmented or informally channeled remittance triggers exchange-infraction fines, possible recharacterization and a bank-side compliance hold on the outgoing wire.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds generated by the CO_SAS in its capacity as an exporter of central-kitchen pastry products, and as the recipient of franchise royalties on the outbound master-franchise model, must be fully canalizada (channeled) through the organized FX market or into a previously registered compensation account. The statutory channeling deadlines are six months from the date of shipment for goods and thirteen months for services and technology or royalty flows. For proceeds equal to or exceeding USD 10,000 per transaction, settlement must pass through an authorized intermediary producing a Declaración de Cambio; sub-threshold proceeds may be received through ordinary local or compensation accounts but remain subject to annual exchange reporting and full traceability. There is no percentage-based mandatory conversion into COP; the legal duty is complete repatriation through regulated rails rather than a fixed composition of currency. The exporter may lawfully hold foreign currency after channeling, but settlement through parallel brokers, unregulated crypto corridors or offshore EMI ledgers constitutes an uncanalized exchange infraction carrying fines, FX-market disqualifications and adverse customs and tax administrative consequences.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow and International-Investment Registration Account (Cuenta de Inversión) plus COP Current Account for operational flows
Capital Escrow Account and Operational COP Account with integrated trade finance
Operational Current Account and USD Compensation Account for cross-border settlements
Capital Escrow and FX hedging counterparty account with structured derivatives coverage
USD Compensation Account and Cross-Border Trade Finance Account
Operational Account and Documentary-Credit (LC) Account for Chinese import settlements
Operational COP Current Account for POS concentration and franchise disbursements
Operational Current Account for payroll and domestic supplier payments
Small-balance Operational Account with limited cross-border capacity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: FEASIBILITY RATING: LOW as a primary treasury rail; LIMITED only as a de-minimis auxiliary collection channel. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise Business, Payoneer and Airwallex are not licensed by the SFC and are not authorized FX market intermediaries under the Colombian exchange regime. They cannot issue legally valid Declaraciones de Cambio, register foreign investment inflows with Banco de la República, or lawfully settle export proceeds in COP. Receiving material foreign funds through such platforms exposes the CO_SAS to uncanalized-flow exchange infractions, loss of the bank-side positive-pay protection, and evidentiary gaps for transfer-pricing and audit defense. Their use is justifiable only for immaterial incidental collections below the USD 10,000 per transaction threshold, provided a written treasury policy designates the EMI as a sub-agent of a tier-1 bank and monthly reconciliation is performed. Locally licensed SEDPEs such as Nequi and Daviplata are permissible solely for domestic low-value COP digital payments covering POS, staff payroll and franchise network disbursements, never for cross-border receipts or conversions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under SFC SARLAFT rules, corporate onboarding requires identification and verification of all legal representatives, signatories and the ultimate beneficial owner being any natural person with direct or indirect participation above 5 percent or exercising control. Physical presence of the appointed legal representative and the beneficial owner at the bank branch with original identification documents is the mainstream and default requirement for the initial corporate KYC interview and the authentication of the account signature card. Some tier-1 banks permit remote onboarding through a supervised videoconference combined with notarized signature certification at a Colombian consulate or before a Colombian public notary, but remote opening is a discretionary exception determined by each bank's AML risk appetite rather than a statutory right. The mandatory documentation backbone includes the notarized incorporation deed, the Chamber of Commerce certificate of existence and legal representation issued within the preceding 30 to 90 days, the notarized board or shareholder minutes appointing the legal representative and approving the account opening, the corporate NIT, the UBO declaration in the SFC-prescribed form, and the completed AML questionnaire. As a conservative treasury-planning measure, the CO_SAS should schedule a physical closing appointment in Bogotá or Medellín for at least one director before any material foreign-capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity in the Chinese master-franchise chain, where the ultimate shareholder appears as a Hong Kong or mainland holding vehicle or as a nominee shareholder, and the natural-person principals are not transparently identifiable in the Colombian Chamber of Commerce register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registers for each holding layer traced up to the final natural persons; a notarized UBO declaration in the SARLAFT format quantifying direct and indirect participation and control; passport copies and identity evidence for each ultimate owner; banking and professional references issued by FATF-compliant institutions; an annotated equity-ownership chart showing voting control and economic entitlement; and the executed master-franchise agreement demonstrating the commercial rationale of the Colombian vehicle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business-model inconsistency where a specialty-bakery entity presents high cash-intense POS takings yet simultaneously requests inbound USD capital subscriptions and recurring outbound royalty wires to a Chinese related party without a documented treasury-flow map or coherent franchise economics.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed treasury-flow diagram covering inbound FDI conversion into COP, daily POS cash sweeps into a single concentration account, supplier payment batches, and quarterly royalty remittances; a pro-forma cash-flow and profit-and-loss bridging the franchise economics; the master-franchise, central-kitchen supply and trademark-license contracts bearing chamber-of-commerce and consular authentication; IFRS journal entries mapping each cash flow to its accounting recognition; and DIAN electronic-invoicing archives evidencing legitimate operational revenues.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list, negative-news or PEP hits on shareholders, signatories or franchise counterparties, including OFAC, UN and EU designations, mainland-Chinese court or graft registries, or any alleged connection to unlicensed casas de cambio and parallel remittance networks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A World-Check or equivalent prescreening report for all UBOs, directors and signatories; a written undertaking to settle exclusively through authorized FX market intermediaries and never through parallel brokers; powers of attorney permitting the bank to conduct periodic re-screening; a documented list of approved FX counterparties; and a group-level AML attestation from the franchisor confirming that all franchisee royalties originate from bank-regulated payment systems.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cold-start entity red flag where the S.A.S. is recently incorporated, the company has no audited financial history, and the board immediately requests a capital escrow account to receive rapid-entry foreign capital from China without prior banking relationships.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The original incorporation deed, the Chamber of Commerce certificate with NIT, the subscribed-and-paid capital records if any; a board-approved business plan aligned with ISIC 5610 and the Chinese-pastry franchise rollout; the central-kitchen and first-store lease agreements; equipment and ingredient pro-forma invoices from Chinese suppliers; a DIAN tax-clearance certificate; a notarized narrative explaining the source and intended traceability of the inbound capital; and an independent accountant's pre-onboarding review of wealth and source-of-funds documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensity and smurfing phenomenology in the bakery franchise network where franchisees make fragmented cash deposits below reporting thresholds across multiple branches and schedules, creating a systemic structuring flag for the consolidated treasury.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full deployment of DIAN-compliant electronic invoicing and certified POS systems at every franchise location; a central cash-concentration agreement requiring same-day electronic sweeps of all store collections into one designated treasury account; the CO_SAS SARLAFT policy setting daily deposit concentration thresholds, detection algorithms and escalation rules; contracts with an armored cash-collection provider; and internal audit evidence confirming the absence of structured cash deposits below the legal reporting thresholds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder or subscribing master-franchisor instructs its offshore bank to transmit USD, EUR or CNH via SWIFT MT103 to the CO_SAS capital account at a tier-1 authorized intermediary. The MT103 must show the true ordering party in field 50K and the exact CO_SAS beneficiary account in field 59, with the payment purpose in fields 72 or 77B stating FDI capital contribution, SARLAFT source verification, and the applicable foreign-investment concept code from the Banco de la República Form No. 5 catalogue for direct-investment cash contributions. For receipts at or above USD 10,000, the intermediary bank generates the Declaración de Cambio and the corresponding exchange registration entry. The bank's compliance gate verifies four elements: the Chamber of Commerce certificate confirming authorized and paid-in capital headroom, the foreign investor appearing in the SAS shareholder register, the remitter identity matching the registered investor under a positive-pay protocol, and the board or shareholder minutes pre-approving the capital subscription or increase. The funds are negotiated into COP at the free market rate if capitalization in COP is elected, and the full principal must be posted to the capital escrow sub-ledger with daily reconciliation. Artificial fragmentation of a single subscription into multiple sub-USD 10,000 tranches is expressly forbidden as exchange fraud; the CO_SAS should bring the full injection in one or a pre-disclosed series of wires and complete the Banco de la República investment registration before any dividend or liquidation distribution is projected.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary outbound rail is the SWIFT MT103 channel for master-franchise royalties and technical-assistance fees payable to the Chinese franchisor; each payment order must cite the underlying royalty invoice, attach the transfer-pricing support file prepared under the TNMM or royalty-comparison method, identify the applicable royalty concept code for technology-transfer and services in the exchange declaration, and undergo dual-signature authorization by the legal representative and the CFO. Commercial settlements for imports of pastry ingredients, custom baking equipment and packaging use documentary letters of credit governed by UCP 600, opened at sight or on a usance basis in USD or CNY, with the full commercial-document package including invoice, bill of lading, phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin and packing list. Documentary collections on a documents-against-payment or documents-against-acceptance basis are employed for recurring consumable imports below USD 25,000 to reduce LC costs. If the CO_SAS maintains a Banco de la República-registered compensation account abroad or in a local USD account, eligible inbound export and royalty receivables may be offset against approved outbound payables only through the periodic canalización reconciliation, never by bypassing the organized FX market; each intercompany invoice is paid gross through a regulated intermediary in accordance with transfer-pricing requirements and Colombian FX law. The bank reviews outbound flows against artificial-benefit pricing and improper valuation indicators before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/COP outright currency forwards contracted with authorized local banks over tenors from one to twenty-four months, supported by documented commercial exposure comprising royalty payables, import payables and export receivables, and executed under an ISDA master or a Colombian-form standard master agreement.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/COP cash-settled in USD or in the COP difference, permissible when the underlying exposure is genuine, identified in the treasury hedge policy and documented for transfer-pricing and tax purposes.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/COP) transacted with tier-1 counterparties for multi-year hedging of royalty streams, central-kitchen capex or foreign-currency financing tenors exceeding one year.

USD/COP currency options comprising calls and puts for contingent hedging of commodity-price movements in pastry inputs and of franchise-capex tender exposures; contracts must be written through supervised financial intermediaries.
Exchange-traded USD/COP futures on the Bolsa de Valores de Colombia (Grupo BVC) with central clearing, used for rolling short-term tactical hedges of seasonal import payment peaks.

FX swaps (spot-forward swaps) executed at local banks to cover temporary liquidity mismatches between same-day COP collections and maturing USD payables while keeping the net currency exposure unchanged.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of mercantile registration (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (local Chamber of Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January – 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal after 31 March triggers a Chamber of Commerce fine of up to approximately USD 250; after two consecutive unrenewed terms, the mercantile registration is cancelled and the company is administratively struck off the registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statement deposit (Depósito de Estados Financieros)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval; for calendar-year companies, by 30 April at the latest
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit prevents renewal of the mercantile registration and renders the corporate books irregular; the company may also lose the evidentiary value of the annual accounts before DIAN until the deposit is completed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 110 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year is the calendar year; Form 110 is due between April and May of the following year according to the DIAN filing calendar based on the last two digits of the NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a fine of 5% of the income tax assessed (minimum 10 UVT) plus DIAN default interest; persistent non-filing can lead to official assessment, enhanced penalties of up to 1.5% of gross revenue, and criminal tax exposure for the legal representative.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and corporate minutes recording (Asamblea General de Accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal body; supporting minutes registered in the Minute Book and any management changes filed with the Cámara de Comercio
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the 31 December year-end, i.e., by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government fine, but unapproved financial statements cannot be validly deposited or used for tax filing; a shareholder may petition judicial convocation, and the Superintendencia de Sociedades may order corrective measures in cases of repeated omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of the Beneficial Ownership Registry (RUB – Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio as administrator of the DIAN-managed UBO registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1–31 August of each year (annual updating window)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is sanctioned under Law 2155 of 2021 with fines ranging in practice from about USD 600 to USD 12,000 depending on severity; the Chamber of Commerce certificate is suspended, affecting banking, notarial and cross-border payment-rail authorizations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Revisor Fiscal (independent statutory auditor) is compulsory when: (i) total assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (approx. COP 7.1 billion / USD 1.7 million in 2025); (ii) gross operating income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV (approx. COP 4.3 billion / USD 1.0 million in 2025); or (iii) shareholders representing at least 5% of subscribed capital request such appointment under Law 43 of 1990 and Law 1258 of 2008. Voluntarily assigned below these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian GAAP for IFRS users per Decree 2420 of 2015 and Decree 2496 of 2015: full IFRS (Group 1), IFRS for SMEs (Group 2), or the micro-entity framework (Group 3). A bakery master-franchise S.A.S. with central kitchen operations normally applies IFRS for SMEs unless public-interest or consolidation thresholds place it in Group 1. Books and supporting documentation must be kept in Spanish; commercial ledgers are retained at least 10 years under Código de Comercio Article 58, while DIAN may verify the last six tax years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every S.A.S. must file the updated UBO information each August through the Cámara de Comercio and maintain the internal Libro de Registro de Accionistas on a continuous basis. Share transfers must be entered in the share register before they can be enforced against the company; any change of beneficial owner during the year must be reported in the next annual RUB confirmation, and the legal representative must certify the full natural-person ownership chain at each confirmation cycle.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea / Junta Directiva)
Register of Directors and Legal Representatives, inclusive of appointment and resignation entries
Diary, general ledger and inventory/balance books duly sealed by the Cámara de Comercio

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–750 per year for registered office address, mail handling, legal proxy and Chamber certificate renewals in Bogotá or Medellín
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–7,000 per year for a certified public accountant or statutory Revisor Fiscal, depending on central kitchen revenue and number of franchised bakery stores

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 5610 bakery franchise operations. General deductions under Colombian tax law may reduce effective burden, including depreciation of productive fixed assets, payroll, social security costs, VAT credits on qualifying capital purchases, and deduction for investments in fixed productive assets under Law 2277/2022.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 - Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (DIAN electronic filing portal, Muisca platform)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, based on the calendar fiscal year (January 1 to December 31)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due between February and April of the following year, determined by the last digit of the taxpayer's NIT under the DIAN filing calendar. For a December 31 year-end, the deadline generally falls no later than April 30 of the succeeding year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross ordinary operating income, including total bakery sales net of VAT and franchise revenue received in Colombia.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for non-residents without a permanent establishment in Colombia; income otherwise subject to final withholding must not be included in Form 110 unless a return is required for refund or special circumstances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs, expenses, and tax credits directly related to the bakery operations, including raw materials, payroll, utilities, rent, franchising royalties paid to unrelated third parties, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents filing only for Colombian-source income may claim allocable deductions only if those deductions are attributable to an in-country permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after application of tax loss carryforwards, statutory deductions, and adjustments required by Colombian tax law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable; non-residents are taxed by final withholding rather than by net taxable income computation where no permanent establishment exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at the 35% statutory rate on net taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A for non-residents subject to final withholding; enter zero if Form 110 is filed for refund purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments, withholding tax credits, excess VAT refunds, and other recoverable credits subtracted from gross income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may include Colombian withholding tax credits only when filing to claim a treaty refund or over-withholding situation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income tax payable or balance due after all credits and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must settle remaining liabilities through the DIAN virtual bank channels; defaults trigger enforcement and collection scenarios.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a monthly surcharge of 0.5% of tax due for each month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of the tax. Incomplete or false returns trigger the 'sanción por inexactitud' equal to 100% of the difference between the tax declared and the tax finally assessed. Criminal tax evasion may additionally lead to imprisonment for 6 to 10 years and fines of up to 150% of the omitted tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders, unless reduced under a double taxation agreement (DTA). Internal dividend distributions between resident companies may be exempt or subject to a different treatment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must (i) obtain a tax residence certificate (TRC) from the treaty-jurisdiction tax authority; (ii) submit the TRC and a beneficial ownership declaration to the Colombian withholding agent prior to payment; (iii) complete the DIAN form or electronic process enabling the reduced withholding rate; and (iv) retain documentary evidence for at least five years for DIAN audit. Failure to provide current documentation results in application of the statutory 20% withholding rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for intellectual property and technical services: statutory withholding rate of 15% (treaty rates may reduce to 0-10% depending on the jurisdiction and beneficial ownership). Interest paid to non-resident creditors: statutory withholding rate of 15% for the gross interest payment; certain treaty jurisdictions qualify for reduced rates. All treaty reductions require a valid TRC and economic-substance assessment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Transfer Pricing Informative Return are required when the taxpayer's gross income or total assets equal or exceed COP 4,706,500,000 (100,000 UVT) and related-party transactions exceed COP 470,650,000 (10,000 UVT) for the taxable year. Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated gross revenue exceeds the DIAN-established threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation as a standalone code, but the DIAN may deny treaty and domestic benefits through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, the beneficial-ownership requirement in DTAs, and the substance-over-form doctrine in Articles 871-1 through 871-5 of the Colombian Tax Code. The tax authority will examine the presence of real offices, qualified payroll, decision-making functions, risk assumption, and commercial substance in the jurisdiction of residence when assessing treaty relief, transfer-pricing structures, and financing or royalty operations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Omission of Cash Sales
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to record cash and POS bakery sales, suppressing a second cash register, overstating raw material purchases, or filing a materially false Form 110.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion under Law 2277/2022: imprisonment of 6 to 10 years and fines of 150% of the omitted tax; civil adjustment of omitted tax plus monthly late interest; loss of deduction rights for the affected fiscal year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The DIAN may pierce the corporate veil and hold directors jointly liable for civil restitution when the evasion was ordered or knowingly tolerated; directors may face travel bans through pending tax claims, disqualification from managing Colombian companies, and criminal imprisonment upon personal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Royalty Drain to Offshore Affiliates
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated royalties or management fees to a non-resident related party without arm's-length support, without Local File documentation, or without demonstrable economic substance at the receiver's side.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may recharacterize the transaction, disallow deductions, assess income tax at 35% on the disallowed amount, apply transfer-pricing penalties and the 100% inaccuracy fine, plus monthly interest from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve unrelated-party arrangements may be personally liable for the underassessment if the transaction was structured solely to strip Colombia-source profit; travel restrictions may be imposed while the case is under investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an S.A.S. entity with minimal capital, no physical premises, no employees, no operational execution, or no corporate substance solely to invoice bakery franchise operations and avoid tax or divert profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The corporate form may be legally disregarded for tax purposes; all income is reallocated to the actual owner or master franchise; threatened penalties under Law 2277/2022 may include penalty of up to 100% of the tax avoided and cancellation of the commercial registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders face civil restitution for unpaid corporate debts when the entity is treated as an alter ego; personal asset attachment and bankruptcy proceedings may be opened; criminal charges for conspiracy to commit tax fraud carry imprisonment up to 12 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Deficiencies in Cash-Intensive Bakery Operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register with the UIAF or failing to file required cash transaction reports, failing to perform customer due diligence on high-value corporate orders, or accepting unusually large cash payments without identification or suspicious-transaction reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Colombian AML law permits fines of up to COP 2,400,000,000 for non-compliant non-regular financial entities; supervisors may order suspension or revocation of the mandatory sanitary and commercial operating license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are subject to personal fines, travel bans during investigation, disqualification from holding public or corporate office, and criminal prosecution for money-laundering facilitation with imprisonment of 10 to 20 years.
